payout_quote: Freelance job boards provide a couple of options for finding freelance graphic designers. The most obvious is posting an ad for a designer.
steps: Create a free Dribbble account and build your profile with shots (work samples).
Browse the Dribbble job board filtered by freelance/remote roles in your discipline.
Read each posting's brief, timeline, and budget.
Apply with a tailored portfolio link, or let clients discover your profile and invite you.
Agree on scope and pay directly with the client; Dribbble is the discovery layer, not the payment processor.
catches: Highly competitive: a huge global designer pool chases the same postings.
Dribbble provides discovery, not escrow — payment terms and collection are on you.
Pay is set per client and varies widely; nothing is standardized.
A thin portfolio gets ignored; you need strong shots to get noticed.
Scam/fake-client risk exists as with any open board — vet before starting work.
biggest_catch: Discovery only, no payment protection: Dribbble connects you to clients but every deal and every dollar is negotiated and collected by you.
eligibility: Free account; designers with a portfolio of work to showcase.
timing: Job board posts continuously; pay per client schedule.

c1.evidence: Dribbble's own career guide (dribbble.com) documents the channel: 'Freelance job boards provide a couple of options for finding freelance graphic designers' and 'you can browse through available freelance graphic designers for hire on Dribbble.'

c2.evidence: Dribbble publishes no payout terms for the board — pay is per client; framed as fully variable.

c3.evidence: Steps follow the documented flow: profile with shots, browse job board, apply or be discovered, deal directly.

c4.evidence: Creating an account and applying are free; no upfront fee documented.

s1.note: Eligibility is a free account with a portfolio.

s2.note: Framed as variable client-set pay; no fixed amount promised.

s3.note: Catches cover competition, no escrow, and variable pay.

s4.note: Deduped: no Dribbble jobs route in qa/existing-providers.txt, dedupe-check.py, or qa/verification/*.json.
